gloss: having an idea; clue; something that comes to mind

definitions.gloss: having an idea; clue; something that comes to mind
definitions.explanation: A vague idea or recollection about something, often used when someone might know the cause, location, or person involved. Frequently used with ある (to have) or ない (to not have).

examples.japanese: {心当|こころあ}たりはありますか。
{犯人|はんにん}に{心当|こころあ}たりがない。
examples.english: I have no idea who the culprit might be.

examples.japanese: {財布|さいふ}をなくした{場所|ばしょ}に{心当|こころあ}たりがあるなら、すぐに{探|さが}しに{行|い}こう。
examples.english: If you have any idea where you lost your wallet, let's go look for it right away.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always appears in the patterns {心当|こころあ}たりがある (to have an idea/clue) or {心当|こころあ}たりがない (to have no idea). Commonly used in conversations about mysteries, lost items, or unknown causes.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {心当|こころあ}たりがある (to have an idea about something)
- {心当|こころあ}たりがない (to have no idea)
- {心当|こころあ}たりはありませんか (do you have any idea? — polite)
- ～に{心当|こころあ}たりがある (to have an idea about ~)
